_comment: Anthropic tool definition. Put it in the `tools` array of a Messages API request. Your code performs the HTTP call when the model emits a tool_use block, and returns the array of records as the tool_result. The description is kept word-for-word identical to the OpenAI one so there is a single wording to maintain.
name: verify_emails
description:
Verify whether email addresses can receive mail. Checks RFC 5322 syntax, DNS/MX records, disposable and role-account lists, then performs a live SMTP handshake with a catch-all probe. Never sends an email. Pass every address from the user's request in one call rather than calling repeatedly. Results come back in a different order than submitted — match them by the `email` field, never by position.

How to read a result:
- deliverable/valid_mailbox: send, the mailbox was confirmed.
- risky/role_based: a shared inbox (info@, support@), not a person.
- risky/catch_all: the domain accepts every address, so this mailbox could not be confirmed.
- risky/free_provider_unverifiable: Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo and iCloud answer the same for every address; the mailbox is unknowable over SMTP.
- risky/full_mailbox: a real mailbox that is over quota; retry in days.
- risky/disposable: a throwaway address; do not send.
- unknown/greylisted: NOT a bad address. The server asked to be retried in 30-60 minutes.
- unknown/smtp_timeout: the server never answered. Unverified, not invalid.
- undeliverable/*: remove the address.

`undeliverable` means the address was found to be dead. `unknown` means the check could not complete. Never report an `unknown` result as invalid or dead.

emails.description: All email addresses to verify in this call.

concurrency.description: Optional. Parallel SMTP sessions, default 15. Leave unset unless the caller asked for a specific rate.
